source.text: Ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐκλεκτῇ κυρίᾳ καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτῆς, οὓς ἐγὼ ἀγαπῶ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ μόνος ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἐγνωκότες τὴν ἀλήθειαν, διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν τὴν μένουσαν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ μεθ’ ἡμῶν ἔσται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα·

records.literal_gloss: The elder to [the] chosen lady and the children of her, whom I love in truth, and not I alone but also all those having known the truth, \v 2 because of the truth the [one] remaining in us, and with us it will be into the age;

en.L: The elder, to [the] chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not I alone but also all who have come to know the truth, \v 2 because of the truth that remains in us and will be with us forever.
en.B: From the elder, to the chosen lady and her children. I love you in truth, and I am not the only one: so do all who have come to know the truth. \v 2 We love you because of the truth that remains in us and will be with us forever.
en.R: This letter is from the elder. It is to the lady whom God has chosen, and to her children. I truly love all of you, and I am not the only one. Everyone who has come to know the truth loves you too. \v 2 We love you because of the truth. The truth remains in us, and it will be with us forever.

es.L: El anciano, a [la] señora escogida y a sus hijos, a los que amo yo en [la] verdad, y no únicamente yo, sino también cuantos han llegado a conocer la verdad, \v 2 por la verdad que permanece en nosotros, y con nosotros estará para siempre.
es.B: Del anciano, a la señora escogida y a sus hijos. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} amo en la verdad, y no soy el único: también {{plural_you:los|os}} aman todos los que han llegado a conocer la verdad. \v 2 {{plural_you:Los|Os}} amamos a causa de la verdad que permanece en nosotros y que estará con nosotros para siempre.
es.R: Esta carta es del anciano. Es para la señora a quien Dios ha escogido, y para sus hijos. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} amo de verdad a todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no soy el único. Todos los que han llegado a conocer la verdad {{plural_you:los|os}} aman también. \v 2 {{plural_you:Los|Os}} amamos a causa de la verdad. La verdad permanece en nosotros, y estará con nosotros para siempre.

fr.L: L’ancien, à la dame élue et à ses enfants, que j’aime en vérité, et non pas moi seul, mais aussi tous ceux qui ont connu la vérité, \v 2 à cause de la vérité qui demeure en nous et qui sera avec nous pour toujours.
fr.B: De la part de l’ancien, à la dame élue et à ses enfants. Je vous aime dans la vérité, et je ne suis pas le seul : tous ceux qui ont appris à connaître la vérité vous aiment aussi. \v 2 Nous vous aimons à cause de la vérité qui demeure en nous et qui sera avec nous pour toujours.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de l’ancien. Elle est pour la dame que Dieu a choisie, et pour ses enfants. Je vous aime tous vraiment, et je ne suis pas le seul. Tous ceux qui ont appris à connaître la vérité vous aiment aussi. \v 2 Nous vous aimons à cause de la vérité. La vérité demeure en nous, et elle sera avec nous pour toujours.

sw.L: Mzee, kwa mama aliyechaguliwa na watoto wake, ambao ninawapenda mimi katika kweli, na si mimi peke yangu, bali pia wote waliokuja kuijua kweli, \v 2 kwa sababu ya kweli inayokaa ndani yetu, na pamoja nasi itakuwa milele.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa mzee, kwa mama aliyechaguliwa na watoto wake. Ninawapenda katika kweli, wala si mimi peke yangu: wote waliokuja kuijua kweli wanawapenda pia. \v 2 Tunawapenda kwa sababu ya kweli inayokaa ndani yetu, nayo itakuwa pamoja nasi milele.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa mzee. Ni kwa mama ambaye Mungu amemchagua, na kwa watoto wake. Ninawapenda ninyi nyote kwa kweli, wala si mimi peke yangu. Kila mtu aliyekuja kuijua kweli anawapenda pia. \v 2 Tunawapenda kwa sababu ya kweli. Kweli hiyo inakaa ndani yetu, nayo itakuwa pamoja nasi milele.

ko.L: 장로가, 택하심을 받은 부인과 그 자녀들에게 [편지합니다]. 나는 여러분을 진리 안에서 사랑합니다. 나만이 아니라 진리를 알게 된 모든 사람도 [여러분을 사랑합니다]. \v 2 우리 안에 머물러 있고 영원히 우리와 함께 있을 그 진리 때문입니다.
ko.B: 장로인 내가, 택하심을 받은 부인과 그 자녀들에게 이 편지를 씁니다. 나는 여러분을 진리 안에서 사랑합니다. 나만이 아니라 진리를 알게 된 모든 사람이 여러분을 사랑합니다. \v 2 우리가 여러분을 사랑하는 것은 우리 안에 머물러 있고 영원히 우리와 함께 있을 진리 때문입니다.
ko.R: 이 편지는 장로인 내가 보냅니다. 하나님께서 택하신 부인과 그 자녀들에게 이 편지를 씁니다. 나는 여러분 모두를 진심으로 사랑합니다. 나만 그런 것이 아닙니다. 진리를 알게 된 사람은 누구나 여러분을 사랑합니다. \v 2 우리가 여러분을 사랑하는 것은 진리 때문입니다. 진리는 우리 안에 머물러 있고, 영원히 우리와 함께 있을 것입니다.

vi.L: Trưởng lão gửi đến bà được chọn và con cái bà, là những người tôi yêu thương trong chân lý, và không phải chỉ một mình tôi, nhưng cả mọi người đã biết chân lý, \v 2 vì cớ chân lý ở trong chúng ta và sẽ ở với chúng ta đời đời.
vi.B: Trưởng lão kính gửi bà được Đức Chúa Trời chọn và con cái bà. Tôi yêu thương bà và con cái bà trong chân lý, và không phải chỉ một mình tôi, mà mọi người đã biết chân lý cũng vậy. \v 2 Chúng tôi yêu thương bà và con cái bà vì cớ chân lý ở trong chúng ta và sẽ ở với chúng ta đời đời.
vi.R: Thư này của trưởng lão. Tôi viết cho bà là người Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn, và cho con cái bà. Tôi thật lòng yêu thương tất cả mọi người trong gia đình bà, và không phải chỉ có tôi. Mọi người đã biết chân lý cũng yêu thương bà và con cái bà. \v 2 Chúng tôi yêu thương bà và con cái bà vì chân lý. Chân lý ở trong chúng ta, và sẽ ở với chúng ta đời đời.

pt.L: O Presbítero, à senhora eleita e aos filhos dela, a quem eu amo em verdade, e não somente eu, mas também todos os que conhecem a verdade, \v 2 por causa da verdade que permanece em nós e estará conosco para sempre.
pt.B: Do Presbítero à senhora eleita e aos filhos dela. Eu amo vocês em verdade, e não sou o único: também os amam todos os que chegaram a conhecer a verdade. \v 2 Nós amamos vocês por causa da verdade que permanece em nós e estará conosco para sempre.
pt.R: Esta carta é do Presbítero. É para a senhora que Deus escolheu e para os filhos dela. Eu amo todos vocês de verdade, e não sou o único. Todos os que chegaram a conhecer a verdade também amam vocês. \v 2 Nós amamos vocês por causa da verdade. A verdade permanece em nós, e vai estar conosco para sempre.

am.L: ሽማግሌው፣ ለተመረጠችው እመቤትና ለልጆቿ፤ እነርሱንም እኔ በእውነት እወዳቸዋለሁ፤ እኔ ብቻ ሳልሆን እውነትን ያወቁ ሁሉ ደግሞ [ይወዷቸዋል]፤ \v 2 [ይህም] በእኛ ስለሚኖረው እውነት ነው፤ [እውነቱም] ለዘላለም ከእኛ ጋር ይሆናል።
am.B: ከሽማግሌው፣ ለተመረጠችው እመቤትና ለልጆቿ። እኔ በእውነት እወዳችኋለሁ፤ የምወዳችሁም እኔ ብቻ አይደለሁም፤ እውነትን ያወቁ ሁሉ ይወዷችኋል። \v 2 የምንወዳችሁ በእኛ ውስጥ ስለሚኖረውና ለዘላለም ከእኛ ጋር ስለሚሆነው እውነት ነው።
am.R: ይህ ደብዳቤ ከሽማግሌው ነው። የምጽፈው እግዚአብሔር ለመረጣት እመቤትና ለልጆቿ ነው። ሁላችሁንም በእውነት እወዳችኋለሁ፤ የምወዳችሁም እኔ ብቻ አይደለሁም። እውነትን ያወቀ ሁሉ ደግሞ ይወዳችኋል። \v 2 የምንወዳችሁ ስለ እውነት ነው። እውነት በእኛ ውስጥ ይኖራል፤ ለዘላለምም ከእኛ ጋር ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: the elder: a title the readers knew, used by the writer in place of his name
alternatives: one of a group of elders who led a local church
decisions.reason: πρεσβύτερος means an older man, and in the churches it named a recognized leader (Acts 14:23; 1 Peter 5:1). With the article and no name, it is a title by which the readers knew the writer at once; 3 John 1 opens the same way. The letter does not name him. Its language is very close to 1 John and John's Gospel, and from the second century the church linked these letters with John; a statement of Papias, preserved by Eusebius, speaks of "the elder John", and whether that is the apostle or another John is debated.

decisions.choice: the chosen lady and her children: a local church and its members, spoken of as a mother and her family
alternatives: a Christian woman and her children (or household)
a woman named Kyria (the Greek word for lady can be a personal name)
decisions.reason: Both readings are possible. For a church: the letter's "you" moves between singular and plural (verses 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 13); its commands (love one another, beware of deceivers, do not receive false teachers) suit a congregation more than one household; the closing greeting comes from the children of her "chosen sister" (verse 13), not from the sister herself, which fits a sister church and its members; and God's people are pictured as a woman elsewhere (Ephesians 5:25-32; Revelation 12; 19:7), with 1 Peter 5:13 sending greetings from "she who is in Babylon, chosen together with you". For a woman: the address reads naturally as a letter to a real person, and the same writer's next letter is to an individual, Gaius (3 John 1). κυρία is the feminine of the word for lord or master and was a polite form of address. The translation keeps "lady" at every level so that the reader can weigh both readings.

decisions.choice: chosen: chosen by God
decisions.reason: ἐκλεκτός is the word for God's chosen people (Romans 8:33; Colossians 3:12; 1 Peter 1:1). The same word describes her sister in verse 13.

decisions.choice: whom I love in truth: a sincere love that belongs to the truth they share
decisions.reason: The relative οὓς is masculine plural and takes in the lady and her children together. ἐν ἀληθείᾳ without the article can mean simply "truly" (as in 3 John 1), but the next words, about all who know the truth and the truth that remains in us, show that the love is grounded in the truth of the gospel. The two senses go together here.

decisions.choice: the shared truth is the reason for the love; the truth that remains now will also be with them forever
alternatives: "because of the truth" begins a new thought joined to the greeting in verse 3
decisions.reason: διὰ gives the ground of the love just described: the elder and all who know the truth love the readers because the same truth lives in all of them. The sentence then changes from a participle ("remaining") to a future verb ("will be"), a promise that the truth will never leave them. "Remain" is the word of 1 John 2:24-27 and John 14:17, where the Spirit of truth remains with the disciples forever.

decisions.choice: the truth: the reality God has made known in Jesus Christ, which believers know and in which they live
decisions.reason: Key term. In John's writings the truth is what God has revealed in Jesus (John 1:14, 17; 14:6), and it remains in believers (1 John 2:4; 2:21). Knowing it is coming to faith; it is the letter's leading word (verses 1-4).

decisions.choice: From the elder; I love you; We love you
alternatives: The elder, to the chosen lady ... whom I love
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long opening into English sentences, as letters open in English: "From ... to ...". "We love you" repeats the subject so that verse 2 can stand as a sentence; "we" is the elder and all who know the truth.

decisions.choice: This letter is from the elder. It is to the lady whom God has chosen; I truly love
alternatives: The elder, to the chosen lady
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that this is the letter's address. "Truly" gives the first sense of "in truth"; the link with the shared truth (meaning decision m4) is carried by the next sentences.

decisions.choice: lady
decisions.reason: "Lady" keeps the open question of meaning decision m2 open at every level. Naming her a church, or reading Kyria as her name, would decide it for the reader; the footnote gives both readings.

decisions.choice: remains
decisions.reason: "Remain" is used for this verb throughout 1 John and here in verse 9. "Abide" is old-fashioned.

decisions.choice: el anciano; la señora escogida
decisions.reason: "Anciano" is the word Spanish uses for the elders of the church, and here it is a title the readers knew (m1); "presbítero" now names a clergy rank. "Señora" is a respectful word for a woman, as the English "lady", and leaves open that she stands for a church (m2).

decisions.choice: en [la] verdad (L); en la verdad (B)
decisions.reason: Without the article, Spanish "en verdad" would read only as "truly". With it, the love belongs to the truth they share (m4), the truth of verses 1-4. Readable says "de verdad", as the English Readable says "truly".

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms for the lady and her children together
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak to the lady and her children together, so each plural "you" is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). Where the letter speaks to the lady alone (verses 4, 5 and 13) Spanish uses "tú", which has no setting.

decisions.choice: l’ancien, lowercase (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The writer names himself by a title the readers knew (m1). French keeps it lowercase, as "les anciens" of the churches elsewhere, so that it reads as a description and not as a proper name; "presbytre" is a technical word few readers know.

decisions.choice: demeurer at every level, as in verse 9 (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in John, "demeurer" is used for this verb in its theological sense, so that verses 2 and 9 and 1 John read alike; the English keeps "remain" at every level.

decisions.choice: mzee; mama aliyechaguliwa
decisions.reason: "Mzee" is the word for a church elder and a title of respect, which fits a title the readers knew (m1). "Mama" is the respectful word for a grown woman, and with "watoto wake" it keeps the picture of a mother and her family that may stand for a church (m2); "bibi" can also mean grandmother. "Aliyechaguliwa" (who has been chosen) says plainly that she was chosen (m3).

decisions.choice: kweli; kukaa
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel and 1 John: "kweli" is the key word for truth (m6), and "kukaa" for the truth that remains in us.

decisions.choice: the letter in 합쇼체 at every level; "부인" for the lady, without "당신", when she is spoken to alone (1:4-5, 13); "여러분" for the plural "you"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the chosen lady and her children as a local church and its members, footnoted. Korean "부인" is the respectful word for a married woman and keeps the picture; a Korean writer addresses such a person by the title itself rather than by a pronoun, so the singular "you" is given as "부인". The plural, the lady with her children, is "여러분", as in the other letters.

decisions.choice: "장로" at every level
decisions.reason: The elder is a title the readers knew, used by the writer in place of his name (meaning decision), so every level keeps the title, as in 1 Peter 5:1.

decisions.choice: "진리" for truth at every level, here "진리 안에서 사랑합니다" (L, B), "진심으로 사랑합니다" (R); "머물러 있다" for remain (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The key Johannine terms are kept as in 1 John and the Korean John: "진리" for truth, "머무르다" for remain. "In truth" is a sincere love that belongs to the truth they share (meaning decision); Readable says "진심으로", as the English Readable says "truly", while the truth itself returns in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: "Trưởng lão" for the elder, who calls himself "tôi"; "bà" for the lady and "con cái bà" for her children; "anh chị em" where the Greek "you" is plural (2:6, 2:8, 2:10, 2:12)
decisions.reason: The chosen lady and her children are most likely a church and its members, spoken of as a mother and her family (m2, uncertain); Vietnamese keeps the picture with "bà", the respectful word for a lady, as the English keeps "lady". Where John turns to the whole church in the plural, he is writing to another church, not to his own children, so the "you" is "anh chị em". "Trưởng lão" is the church title of 1 Peter 5:1.

decisions.choice: "chân lý" for the truth and "ở trong" for remaining, as in 1 John
decisions.reason: The truth is the reality God has made known in Jesus Christ (m6), and "remain" is the word of 1 John 2:6; the letter keeps the same Vietnamese key terms.

decisions.choice: o Presbítero, capitalized, at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole letter, and as in 3 John 1. The writer uses the title in place of his name, and the readers knew him by it (meaning decision m1), so Portuguese writes it as a title with a capital. "Presbítero" is the word style section 6 uses for church elders; "ancião" is kept for Jewish elders, and "o velho" would lose the sense of a recognized leader.

decisions.choice: à senhora eleita (L, B); à senhora que Deus escolheu (R)
decisions.reason: As the English "lady", "senhora" keeps open the question in meaning decision m2, whether a church or a woman is meant; naming a church or reading Kyria as her name would decide it, and the footnote gives both readings. "Eleita" is the word for God's chosen people (m3); Readable says who chose her, as the English does.

decisions.choice: em verdade
decisions.reason: "Na verdade" is an everyday Portuguese phrase for "actually", which would make the elder say "whom I actually love"; "em verdade" keeps both senses of meaning decision m4, a sincere love and a love that belongs to the truth they share.

decisions.choice: ሽማግሌው (the elder); ለተመረጠችው እመቤት (to the chosen lady); the lady addressed as አንቺ (singular, verses 4, 5, 13) and the church as እናንተ (plural, verses 6, 8, 10, 12)
decisions.reason: "ሽማግሌ" is the word for the church office of elder in the Amharic of Paul's letters (Titus 1:5), and with the definite suffix it is a title the readers knew (meaning decision m1); a church title such as "ቀሲስ" would name a later office. The lady stands for a local church and her children for its members (m2), so "እመቤት" keeps the picture of a mother and her household. Amharic, like Greek, tells singular and plural "you" apart, so the reader can follow the elder's turns between the lady and her children.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: the pronouns for God in this letter are written once
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the letter, as in 1 John.

source.text: ἔσται μεθ’ ἡμῶν χάρις ἔλεος εἰρήνη παρὰ θεοῦ πατρός, καὶ παρὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ πατρός, ἐν ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀγάπῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Will be with us grace, mercy, peace from God [the] Father, and from Jesus Christ the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

en.L: Grace, mercy, [and] peace will be with us from God [the] Father and from Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
en.B: Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us from God the Father and from Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Father's Son, in truth and love.
en.R: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Father's Son, will be with us as we live in truth and love.

es.L: Estarán con nosotros gracia, misericordia [y] paz de parte de Dios Padre y de parte de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el Hijo del Padre, en verdad y amor.
es.B: Gracia, misericordia y paz estarán con nosotros de parte de Dios Padre y de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el Hijo del Padre, en la verdad y el amor.
es.R: La gracia, la misericordia y la paz de Dios Padre y de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el Hijo del Padre, estarán con nosotros mientras vivimos en la verdad y en el amor.

fr.L: Grâce, miséricorde [et] paix seront avec nous de la part de Dieu [le] Père et de la part de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le Fils du Père, dans la vérité et l’amour.
fr.B: Grâce, miséricorde et paix seront avec nous de la part de Dieu le Père et de la part de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, le Fils du Père, dans la vérité et l’amour.
fr.R: La grâce, la miséricorde et la paix qui viennent de Dieu le Père et de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, le Fils du Père, seront avec nous pendant que nous vivons dans la vérité et dans l’amour.

sw.L: Zitakuwa pamoja nasi neema, rehema [na] amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba, na kutoka kwa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} aliye Mwana wa Baba, katika kweli na upendo.
sw.B: Neema, rehema na amani zitakuwa pamoja nasi kutoka kwa Mungu Baba na kutoka kwa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Baba, katika kweli na upendo.
sw.R: Neema, rehema na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba na kutoka kwa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Baba, zitakuwa pamoja nasi tunapoishi katika kweli na upendo.

ko.L: 은혜와 긍휼과 평안이 하나님 아버지와 아버지의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에게서 진리와 사랑 안에서 우리와 함께 있을 것입니다.
ko.B: 하나님 아버지와 아버지의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 주시는 은혜와 긍휼과 평안이 진리와 사랑 안에서 우리와 함께 있을 것입니다.
ko.R: 우리가 진리와 사랑 안에서 살 때, 하나님 아버지와 아버지의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 주시는 은혜와 긍휼과 평안이 우리와 함께 있을 것입니다.

vi.L: Ân điển, lòng thương xót [và] bình an từ Đức Chúa Trời là Cha và từ Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, Con của Cha, sẽ ở cùng chúng ta trong chân lý và tình yêu thương.
vi.B: Ân điển, lòng thương xót và bình an từ Đức Chúa Trời là Cha và từ Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, Con của Cha, sẽ ở cùng chúng ta trong chân lý và tình yêu thương.
vi.R: Ân điển, lòng thương xót và bình an từ Đức Chúa Trời là Cha, và từ Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, Con của Cha, sẽ ở cùng chúng ta khi chúng ta sống trong chân lý và tình yêu thương.

pt.L: Graça, misericórdia [e] paz estarão conosco da parte de Deus Pai e da parte de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, o Filho do Pai, em verdade e amor.
pt.B: Graça, misericórdia e paz estarão conosco da parte de Deus Pai e de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, o Filho do Pai, em verdade e amor.
pt.R: A graça, a misericórdia e a paz que vêm de Deus Pai e de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, o Filho do Pai, estarão conosco enquanto vivermos na verdade e no amor.

am.L: ጸጋ፣ ምሕረት፣ ሰላም ከእግዚአብሔር አብና ከአብ ልጅ ከኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በእውነትና በፍቅር ከእኛ ጋር ይሆናል።
am.B: ጸጋ፣ ምሕረትና ሰላም ከእግዚአብሔር አብና ከአብ ልጅ ከኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በእውነትና በፍቅር ከእኛ ጋር ይሆናሉ።
am.R: ከእግዚአብሔር አብና ከአብ ልጅ ከኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} የሚመጣው ጸጋ፣ ምሕረትና ሰላም በእውነትና በፍቅር ስንኖር ከእኛ ጋር ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: a confident promise: grace, mercy and peace will be with us
alternatives: a wish: may grace, mercy and peace be with us
decisions.reason: Letter greetings usually have no verb ("grace to you") or a wish. Here the verb is future, ἔσται, picking up "will be with us" at the end of verse 2. The elder states what will be, and he includes himself ("us").

decisions.choice: grace, mercy, peace: God's undeserved favor, his compassion toward the needy, and the wholeness he gives
alternatives: three ways of saying the same thing
decisions.reason: Key terms grace and peace. The same three words open 1 Timothy 1:2 and 2 Timothy 1:2; ἔλεος adds God's pity for those who cannot help themselves. Together they name what comes from God and his Son.

decisions.choice: grace comes from the Father and from Jesus Christ alike; he is the Son of the Father
alternatives: the Son as only a channel of the Father's gifts
decisions.reason: The preposition παρὰ is repeated before Jesus Christ, so both are named as the source. "The Son of the Father" is found only here in the New Testament; it ties Jesus to the Father as the letter does again in verse 9 ("has both the Father and the Son").

decisions.choice: in truth and love: the setting in which these gifts are known, the truth believed and the love lived out
alternatives: describing God's way of giving them
decisions.reason: Truth and love are the two themes of the letter (truth in verses 1-4; love in verses 5-6). The gifts are enjoyed where the truth is held and love is practiced.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "with us", and "from Jesus Christ"
alternatives: "from the Lord Jesus Christ" (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "with you", the form a greeting usually takes; many later manuscripts add "Lord" before Jesus Christ, as in most New Testament greetings. The SBLGNT follows manuscripts with the less usual forms. The meaning changes little. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: Grace, mercy, [and] peace will be with us
alternatives: Will be with us grace, mercy, peace
decisions.reason: English needs the subject before the verb; Literal moves the three words forward and brackets "and".

decisions.choice: the Father's Son
decisions.reason: Shorter and natural; Literal keeps the Greek form.

decisions.choice: as we live in truth and love
decisions.reason: Readable says how "in truth and love" relates to the gifts (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in 1 John and Jude, the default is the usual Spanish name "Jesucristo", and the alternative separates name and title.

decisions.choice: "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L); "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R); "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" with the article outside the span (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: no hyphen, so that both options read naturally; the article French needs before the title stays outside the span (verse 9). "L’antichrist" in verse 7 takes no setting, as in the English.

decisions.choice: Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}; no deity_pronoun spans in prefixes
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in 1 John: Swahili has no article, so "Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}" reads naturally either way. Pronouns for God are mostly inside the verb, where a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns and possessives (verse 6, "zake").

decisions.choice: "은혜와 긍휼과 평안 ... 있을 것입니다" (a promise)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the greeting as a confident promise, not a wish, so Korean says "있을 것입니다". The three words are the key terms of the greetings in the other letters: "은혜", "긍휼" and "평안".

decisions.choice: ይሆናል (will be), a promise, not ይሁን (may it be)
alternatives: ይሁን, the wish of Paul's greetings
decisions.reason: Most letter greetings are wishes, and the Amharic of Paul's letters says "ይሁን". Here the Greek has a future, a confident promise (meaning decision m1), so Amharic says "ይሆናል". "ምሕረት" is God's compassion toward the needy (m2), beside "ጸጋ" and "ሰላም" of the table.

source.text: Ἐχάρην λίαν ὅτι εὕρηκα ἐκ τῶν τέκνων σου περιπατοῦντας ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, καθὼς ἐντολὴν ἐλάβομεν παρὰ τοῦ πατρός.

records.literal_gloss: I rejoiced greatly that I have found [some] of the children of you walking in truth, just as commandment we received from the Father.

en.L: I rejoiced greatly that I have found [some] of your children walking in truth, just as we received [a] command from the Father.
en.B: I was very glad when I found some of your children living in the truth, in keeping with the command we received from the Father.
en.R: I was very happy to find out that some of your children are living by the truth. That is what the Father commanded us to do.

es.L: Me alegré mucho de haber encontrado a [algunos] de tus hijos andando en [la] verdad, tal como recibimos mandamiento del Padre.
es.B: Me alegré muchísimo al encontrar a algunos de tus hijos viviendo en la verdad, de acuerdo con el mandamiento que el Padre nos dio.
es.R: Me puse muy contento al saber que algunos de tus hijos viven según la verdad. Eso es lo que el Padre nos mandó hacer.

fr.L: Je me suis beaucoup réjoui d’avoir trouvé [certains] de tes enfants marchant dans la vérité, selon le commandement que nous avons reçu du Père.
fr.B: J’ai été très heureux de trouver certains de tes enfants qui vivent dans la vérité, selon le commandement que nous avons reçu du Père.
fr.R: J’ai été très content d’apprendre que certains de tes enfants vivent selon la vérité. C’est ce que le Père nous a commandé de faire.

sw.L: Nilifurahi mno kwamba nimewakuta [baadhi] ya watoto wako wakitembea katika kweli, sawasawa na amri tuliyopokea kutoka kwa Baba.
sw.B: Nilifurahi sana nilipowakuta baadhi ya watoto wako wakiishi katika kweli, kwa kufuata amri tuliyopokea kutoka kwa Baba.
sw.R: Nilifurahi sana kujua kwamba baadhi ya watoto wako wanaishi kwa kufuata kweli. Hivyo ndivyo Baba alivyotuamuru tufanye.

ko.L: 우리가 아버지께로부터 계명을 받은 대로, 부인의 자녀들 가운데 진리 안에서 걷는 이들을 내가 보게 되어 매우 기뻤습니다.
ko.B: 우리가 아버지께 받은 계명대로, 부인의 자녀들 가운데 몇 사람이 진리 안에서 살고 있는 것을 보고 나는 매우 기뻤습니다.
ko.R: 부인의 자녀들 가운데 몇 사람이 진리대로 살고 있다는 것을 알게 되어 나는 매우 기뻤습니다. 그것이 바로 아버지께서 우리에게 명령하신 것입니다.

vi.L: Tôi rất vui mừng vì đã thấy [một số] con cái của bà bước đi trong chân lý, đúng như điều răn chúng ta đã nhận từ Cha.
vi.B: Tôi rất vui khi thấy một số con cái của bà sống theo chân lý, đúng như điều răn chúng ta đã nhận từ Cha.
vi.R: Tôi rất vui khi biết rằng một số con cái của bà đang sống theo chân lý. Đó là điều Cha đã truyền cho chúng ta phải làm.

pt.L: Alegrei-me muito por ter encontrado [alguns] dos seus filhos andando em verdade, assim como recebemos [o] mandamento da parte do Pai.
pt.B: Fiquei muito contente quando encontrei alguns dos seus filhos vivendo na verdade, de acordo com o mandamento que recebemos do Pai.
pt.R: Fiquei muito feliz ao saber que alguns dos seus filhos estão vivendo de acordo com a verdade. Foi isso que o Pai nos mandou fazer.

am.L: ከልጆችሽ አንዳንዶቹ ከአብ ትእዛዝ እንደ ተቀበልን በእውነት ሲመላለሱ ስላገኘሁ እጅግ ደስ አለኝ።
am.B: ከአብ በተቀበልነው ትእዛዝ መሠረት ከልጆችሽ አንዳንዶቹ በእውነት ሲመላለሱ ባገኘሁ ጊዜ እጅግ ደስ አለኝ።
am.R: ከልጆችሽ አንዳንዶቹ በእውነት እንደሚኖሩ ስላወቅኩ በጣም ደስ አለኝ። አብ እንድናደርግ ያዘዘን ይህንኑ ነው።

decisions.choice: some of your children: those the elder has met, without implying anything about the others
alternatives: only some, because the others were not living in the truth
decisions.reason: ἐκ before "the children" means some of them. The elder may simply have met some, perhaps on their travels; the letter does not say the rest had gone astray, though the warnings of verses 7-11 show the danger was real.

decisions.choice: your: the lady, addressed in the singular
decisions.reason: σου is singular, as are the forms for "you" in verse 5. Verse 6 moves to the plural (see the decision there).

decisions.choice: walking in truth: living their lives by the truth
decisions.reason: To walk is a Hebrew way of speaking of how one lives (1 John 1:6-7; 2:6; 3 John 3-4). "In truth" (key term) is the truth of verses 1-2: they live by what God has made known.

decisions.choice: the command from the Father: to believe in his Son and love one another
decisions.reason: "We received" takes in the elder and all believers. 1 John 3:23 states the Father's command in these terms, and verses 5-6 here go on to name love.

decisions.choice: living (B); living by (R)
decisions.reason: "Walking" for a way of life is church language; Balanced and Readable say "living", as 1 John 2:6 does. Literal keeps the image.

decisions.choice: I was very glad (B); I was very happy (R)
decisions.reason: Natural English for the aorist verb of rejoicing. The word is not the noun joy (key term), which comes in verse 12.

decisions.choice: tú for the lady
decisions.reason: The elder writes to the lady in the singular (m2), with warmth. Spanish uses "tú" for her, as it does when Jesus speaks to one person; "usted" would sound distant in a letter of love. The singular has no reader setting.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: A letter speaks to its readers, so French uses the passé composé for what has happened ("je me suis réjoui", "nous avons reçu"), as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: "tu" to the lady (verses 4, 5, 13); "vous" where the Greek turns to the plural (verses 1, 6, 8, 10, 12) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French can show the shift English hides (m2; verse 6 m4): the elder addresses the lady alone, then her and her children together.

decisions.choice: wakitembea (L); wakiishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of walking with the everyday verb "kutembea"; Balanced and Readable say "kuishi" (live), as the English says "living" (m3).

decisions.choice: seus (você, singular), then vocês from verse 6
decisions.reason: The elder writes to the lady in the singular here and in verse 5 (meaning decision m2), and Portuguese uses "você" with "seu/sua" and "lhe", as style section 4 has it between people; "a senhora" as a pronoun would blur with the title "senhora", and "tu" is kept for God and Jesus. From verse 6 the plural is "vocês", and the closing greeting (verse 13) returns to "você".

source.text: καὶ νῦν ἐρωτῶ σε, κυρία, οὐχ ὡς ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφων σοι ἀλλὰ ἣν εἴχομεν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους.

records.literal_gloss: And now I ask you, lady, not as a commandment new writing to you but [one] which we had from [the] beginning, that we love one another.

en.L: And now I ask you, lady, not as writing to you a new command, but [the one] that we have had from [the] beginning: that we love one another.
en.B: And now, lady, I have a request for you. What I am writing to you is not a new command; it is the one we have had from the beginning. I ask that we love one another.
en.R: And now, dear lady, I am asking you something. I am not writing to give you a new command. It is the command we have had from the very beginning: we must love one another.

es.L: Y ahora te pido, señora, no como quien te escribe un mandamiento nuevo, sino aquel que teníamos desde [el] principio: que nos amemos unos a otros.
es.B: Y ahora, señora, tengo algo que pedirte. Lo que te escribo no es un mandamiento nuevo; es el que hemos tenido desde el principio. Te pido que nos amemos unos a otros.
es.R: Y ahora, querida señora, quiero pedirte algo. No te escribo para darte un mandamiento nuevo. Es el mandamiento que hemos tenido desde el mismo principio: debemos amarnos unos a otros.

fr.L: Et maintenant je te demande, dame, non comme t’écrivant un commandement nouveau, mais celui que nous avions dès le commencement : que nous nous aimions les uns les autres.
fr.B: Et maintenant, chère dame, j’ai une demande à te faire. Ce que je t’écris n’est pas un commandement nouveau : c’est celui que nous avons depuis le commencement. Je demande que nous nous aimions les uns les autres.
fr.R: Et maintenant, chère dame, je te demande quelque chose. Je ne t’écris pas pour te donner un commandement nouveau. C’est le commandement que nous avons depuis le tout début : nous devons nous aimer les uns les autres.

sw.L: Na sasa nakusihi, mama, si kwa kukuandikia amri mpya, bali [amri] tuliyokuwa nayo tangu mwanzo, kwamba tupendane.
sw.B: Na sasa, mama, nina ombi kwako. Ninachokuandikia si amri mpya; ni ile ambayo tumekuwa nayo tangu mwanzo. Ninaomba tupendane.
sw.R: Na sasa, mama mpendwa, ninakuomba jambo moja. Sikuandikii ili nikupe amri mpya. Ni amri ambayo tumekuwa nayo tangu mwanzo kabisa: tunapaswa kupendana.

ko.L: 그리고 이제 부인, 내가 부인께 부탁합니다. 내가 부인께 새 계명을 쓰는 것이 아니라 우리가 처음부터 가지고 있던 [계명을 씁니다]. 곧 우리가 서로 사랑하자는 것입니다.
ko.B: 이제 부인께 부탁할 것이 있습니다. 내가 쓰는 것은 새 계명이 아니라 우리가 처음부터 가지고 있던 계명입니다. 우리가 서로 사랑하자는 것입니다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 부인, 이제 부인께 부탁할 것이 있습니다. 나는 새 계명을 주려고 이 편지를 쓰는 것이 아닙니다. 그것은 우리가 맨 처음부터 가지고 있던 계명입니다. 우리는 서로 사랑해야 합니다.

vi.L: Và bây giờ, thưa bà, tôi xin bà, không phải như viết cho bà một điều răn mới, nhưng là [điều răn] chúng ta đã có từ ban đầu: chúng ta hãy yêu thương nhau.
vi.B: Và bây giờ, thưa bà, tôi có một lời xin với bà. Điều tôi viết cho bà không phải là một điều răn mới; đó là điều răn chúng ta đã có từ ban đầu. Tôi xin rằng chúng ta hãy yêu thương nhau.
vi.R: Và bây giờ, thưa bà, tôi xin bà một điều. Tôi không viết để ban cho bà một điều răn mới. Đó là điều răn chúng ta đã có ngay từ lúc ban đầu: chúng ta phải yêu thương nhau.

pt.L: E agora lhe peço, senhora, não como se lhe escrevesse um mandamento novo, mas [aquele] que temos desde [o] princípio: que amemos uns aos outros.
pt.B: E agora, senhora, tenho um pedido a lhe fazer. O que escrevo a você não é um mandamento novo; é o que temos desde o princípio. Peço que amemos uns aos outros.
pt.R: E agora, querida senhora, estou pedindo uma coisa a você. Não estou escrevendo para dar a você um mandamento novo. É o mandamento que temos desde o começo: precisamos amar uns aos outros.

am.L: አሁንም እመቤት ሆይ፣ አዲስ ትእዛዝ እንደምጽፍልሽ ሳይሆን ከመጀመሪያ ጀምሮ የነበረንን [ትእዛዝ] እለምንሻለሁ፤ እርስ በርሳችን እንድንዋደድ።
am.B: አሁንም እመቤት ሆይ፣ አንድ ልመና አለኝ። የምጽፍልሽ አዲስ ትእዛዝ አይደለም፤ ከመጀመሪያ ጀምሮ የነበረን ትእዛዝ ነው። እርስ በርሳችን እንድንዋደድ እለምንሻለሁ።
am.R: አሁንም ውድ እመቤት ሆይ፣ አንድ ነገር እጠይቅሻለሁ። የምጽፍልሽ አዲስ ትእዛዝ ልሰጥሽ አይደለም። ገና ከመጀመሪያው ጀምሮ የነበረን ትእዛዝ ነው፤ እርስ በርሳችን መዋደድ አለብን።

decisions.choice: ask: a personal request, though what is asked is a command
decisions.reason: ἐρωτάω is the ordinary verb for asking. The elder appeals rather than orders, yet he is careful to say that what he asks is the command they already have.

decisions.choice: you, lady: still the singular
decisions.reason: σε and σοι are singular and κυρία is a direct address. Whether she is a church or a woman, the request is put to her; its content, "that we love one another", takes in everyone (meaning decision m2 in verse 1).

decisions.choice: from the beginning: since the readers first heard the gospel
decisions.reason: The same words in 1 John 2:7, 24 and 3:11 refer to what the readers heard when they first believed. It is the command Jesus gave (John 13:34-35; 15:12, 17).

decisions.choice: that we love one another: both what the elder asks and what the command says
decisions.reason: The clause with ἵνα follows the verb "ask" and gives the request; it is also the content of the old command, exactly as in 1 John 3:11.

decisions.choice: dear lady
decisions.reason: In English "lady" alone as an address sounds abrupt. Readable adds the warmth the letter shows; Literal and Balanced keep the plain word.

decisions.choice: I have a request for you; I ask that
alternatives: I ask you ... not as writing ... that we love one another
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the sentence in three and repeats "ask" before the request so the reader does not lose the thread.

decisions.choice: dame (L); chère dame (B, R)
decisions.reason: Bare "dame" as a form of address is archaic in French, and "Madame" would clash with "tu". "Chère dame" is warm and natural, as the English Readable's "dear lady"; Literal keeps the plain word.

source.text: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγάπη, ἵνα περιπατῶμεν κατὰ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ· αὕτη ἡ ἐντολή ἐστιν, καθὼς ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῇ περιπατῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: And this is the love, that we walk according to the commandments of him; this the commandment is, just as you heard from [the] beginning, that in it you walk.

en.L: And this is love: that we walk according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. This is the command, just as you heard from [the] beginning: that you walk in it.
en.B: This is what love is: that we live by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. And this is the command you heard from the beginning: you are to live in love.
en.R: Loving means living the way God commands us to live. And God's command, the one you heard from the very beginning, is that you live a life of love.

es.L: Y el amor es este: que andemos conforme a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos. Este es el mandamiento, tal como {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde [el] principio: que {{plural_you:anden|andéis}} en él.
es.B: Esto es el amor: que vivamos según {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos. Y este es el mandamiento que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde el principio: que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}} en el amor.
es.R: Amar es vivir como Dios nos manda vivir. Y el mandamiento de Dios, el que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde el mismo principio, es que {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} una vida de amor.

fr.L: Et voici l’amour : que nous marchions selon {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements. Voici le commandement, comme vous l’avez entendu dès le commencement : que vous y marchiez.
fr.B: Voici ce qu’est l’amour : vivre selon {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements. Et voici le commandement que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement : vous devez vivre dans l’amour.
fr.R: Aimer, c’est vivre comme Dieu nous commande de vivre. Et le commandement de Dieu, celui que vous avez entendu depuis le tout début, c’est que vous viviez dans l’amour.

sw.L: Na upendo ni huu, kwamba tutembee kufuatana na amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Amri ni hii, kama mlivyosikia tangu mwanzo, kwamba mtembee ndani yake.
sw.B: Upendo ndio huu: kwamba tuishi kwa kufuata amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Na amri mliyoisikia tangu mwanzo ni hii: mnapaswa kuishi katika upendo.
sw.R: Kupenda ni kuishi kama Mungu anavyotuamuru tuishi. Na amri ya Mungu, ile mliyoisikia tangu mwanzo kabisa, ni kwamba muishi maisha ya upendo.

ko.L: 그리고 사랑은 이것이니, 곧 우리가 그분의 계명들을 따라 걷는 것입니다. 여러분이 처음부터 들은 대로, 계명은 이것이니, 곧 여러분이 그 안에서 걷는 것입니다.
ko.B: 사랑은 이것입니다. 우리가 그분의 계명대로 사는 것입니다. 그리고 여러분이 처음부터 들은 계명은 이것입니다. 여러분은 사랑 안에서 살아야 합니다.
ko.R: 사랑한다는 것은 하나님께서 명령하신 대로 사는 것입니다. 그리고 여러분이 맨 처음부터 들은 하나님의 계명은 여러분이 사랑하며 사는 것입니다.

vi.L: Và đây là tình yêu thương: chúng ta bước đi theo các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Đây là điều răn, như anh chị em đã nghe từ ban đầu: anh chị em phải bước đi trong đó.
vi.B: Tình yêu thương là thế này: chúng ta sống theo các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Và đây là điều răn anh chị em đã nghe từ ban đầu: anh chị em phải sống trong tình yêu thương.
vi.R: Yêu thương nghĩa là sống theo cách Đức Chúa Trời truyền dạy chúng ta. Và điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời, là điều anh chị em đã nghe ngay từ lúc ban đầu, là anh chị em phải sống một đời sống yêu thương.

pt.L: E este é o amor: que andemos segundo os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} mandamentos. Este é o mandamento, assim como vocês ouviram desde [o] princípio: que andem nele.
pt.B: Isto é o amor: que vivamos segundo os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} mandamentos. E este é o mandamento que vocês ouviram desde o princípio: que vivam no amor.
pt.R: Amar é viver do jeito que Deus nos manda viver. E o mandamento de Deus, aquele que vocês ouviram desde o começo, é que vocês vivam uma vida de amor.

am.L: ፍቅርም ይህ ነው፤ እንደ ትእዛዛቱ እንድንመላለስ። ትእዛዙ ይህ ነው፤ ከመጀመሪያ እንደ ሰማችሁት በእርሱ እንድትመላለሱ።
am.B: ፍቅር ማለት ይህ ነው፤ በትእዛዛቱ መሠረት መመላለስ። ከመጀመሪያ ጀምሮ የሰማችሁትም ትእዛዝ ይህ ነው፤ በፍቅር እንድትመላለሱ።
am.R: መውደድ ማለት እግዚአብሔር እንዳዘዘን መኖር ማለት ነው። ገና ከመጀመሪያው የሰማችሁት የእግዚአብሔር ትእዛዝም በፍቅር እንድትኖሩ ነው።

decisions.choice: love is shown in living by God's commands
alternatives: love as a feeling apart from obedience
decisions.reason: The same link is made in 1 John 5:3 and John 14:15, 21. The love of verse 5 is not only a feeling; it is a way of life shaped by what God commands.

decisions.choice: his: God the Father's
decisions.reason: The Father has just been named as the one who gave the command (verse 4). In John's writings the commands of the Father and of the Son are the same commands.

decisions.choice: in it: in love
decisions.reason: αὐτῇ is feminine and can stand for love (ἀγάπη) or the command (ἐντολή), both feminine. Walking in love gives a full circle: love means keeping the commands, and the command is to walk in love. Walking "in the command" would be an unusual expression, though the sense comes close.

decisions.choice: you: now plural, the lady and her children together
decisions.reason: From here on the elder writes "you" in the plural (verses 8, 10, 12), returning to the singular only in the closing greeting (verse 13). The commands are for every member; this switching is one of the reasons the lady is often taken to be a church (meaning decision m2 in verse 1).

decisions.choice: live (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4: walking is a picture of how one lives. Literal keeps "walk".

decisions.choice: in love (B); a life of love (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "it" refers to (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "in it", which the footnote explains.

decisions.choice: God commands; God's command
decisions.reason: Readable names God (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: en él
decisions.reason: "It" most likely means love, but the Greek does not settle it (m3). Spanish "amor" and "mandamiento" are both masculine, so Literal "en él" keeps the question open, as the Greek does; Balanced and Readable say "love", as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: Every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the span, as in Colossians; the possessive agrees with "commandements".

decisions.choice: que vous y marchiez (L)
decisions.reason: "It" may be love or the command (m3). "Y" leaves the question open as the Greek does; "en lui" could be read as Christ, and "en elle" would point to nothing in French, where both nouns are masculine.

decisions.choice: ndani yake
decisions.reason: "It" most likely means love, but the Greek does not settle it (m3). Literal "ndani yake" can point to love or to the command, as the Greek can; Balanced and Readable say "upendo", as the English says "love".

decisions.choice: "그 안에서" (L); "사랑 안에서" (B); "사랑하며" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "in it" as in love and footnotes the reading "in the command". Literal keeps the open pronoun; Balanced and Readable name love, as the English Balanced and Readable do.

decisions.choice: nele
decisions.reason: The Greek feminine pronoun can stand for love or for the command (meaning decision m3). Portuguese "amor" and "mandamento" are both masculine, so "nele" keeps the same openness at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "no amor", as the English does.

decisions.choice: መመላለስ (walk, L, B), መኖር (live, R), as in 1 John 1:6-7; በእርሱ (in it, L), በፍቅር (in love, B, R)
decisions.reason: To walk is to live (meaning decision m1), and the Amharic keeps the words of 1 John for it. Literal keeps the Greek pronoun; Balanced and Readable say what it points to, love (m3). From here the verbs are plural, "እናንተ", as the Greek turns to the lady and her children together (m4).

source.text: ὅτι πολλοὶ πλάνοι ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸν κόσμον, οἱ μὴ ὁμολογοῦντες Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐρχόμενον ἐν σαρκί· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πλάνος καὶ ὁ ἀντίχριστος.

records.literal_gloss: Because many deceivers went out into the world, those not confessing Jesus Christ coming in flesh; this is the deceiver and the antichrist.

en.L: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} coming in [the] flesh. This one is the deceiver and the antichrist.
en.B: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, people who do not confess Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as one who has come in the flesh. A person like that is the deceiver and the antichrist.
en.R: This matters, because many people who lead others astray have gone out into the world. They will not openly say that Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came as a real human being. A person like that is the deceiver and the antichrist, the enemy of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Porque muchos engañadores han salido al mundo, los que no confiesan a {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} viniendo en carne. Este es el engañador y el anticristo.
es.B: Porque muchos engañadores han salido al mundo, gente que no confiesa a {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} como aquel que ha venido en la carne. Alguien así es el engañador y el anticristo.
es.R: Esto es importante, porque muchas personas que apartan a otros del camino han salido al mundo. No quieren decir abiertamente que {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} vino como un ser humano de verdad. Alguien así es el engañador y el anticristo, el enemigo {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

fr.L: Car beaucoup de trompeurs sont sortis dans le monde, ceux qui ne confessent pas Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} venant dans la chair. Celui-là est le trompeur et l’antichrist.
fr.B: Car beaucoup de trompeurs se sont répandus dans le monde : des gens qui ne confessent pas Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} comme venu dans la chair. Une personne de ce genre, c’est le trompeur et l’antichrist.
fr.R: C’est important, car beaucoup de gens qui égarent les autres se sont répandus dans le monde. Ils refusent de dire ouvertement que Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est venu comme un vrai être humain. Une personne comme celle-là, c’est le trompeur et l’antichrist, l’ennemi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu wapotoshaji wengi wametoka kwenda ulimwenguni, wale wasiomkiri Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} akija katika mwili. Huyu ndiye mpotoshaji na mpinga-Kristo.
sw.B: Kwa maana wapotoshaji wengi wametoka kwenda ulimwenguni, watu wasiomkiri Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kuwa amekuja katika mwili. Mtu wa namna hiyo ndiye mpotoshaji na mpinga-Kristo.
sw.R: Jambo hili ni muhimu, kwa sababu watu wengi wanaowapotosha wengine wametoka kwenda ulimwenguni. Hawataki kusema waziwazi kwamba Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikuja kama binadamu halisi. Mtu wa namna hiyo ndiye mpotoshaji na mpinga-Kristo, adui wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

ko.L: 많은 미혹하는 자들이 세상에 나왔기 때문입니다. 그들은 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 육신으로 오심을 시인하지 않는 사람들입니다. 이런 사람이 미혹하는 자요 적그리스도입니다.
ko.B: 많은 미혹하는 사람들이 세상에 나왔기 때문입니다. 그들은 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 육신을 입고 오신 분이심을 시인하지 않습니다. 이런 사람이 바로 미혹하는 자이며 적그리스도입니다.
ko.R: 이것이 중요한 까닭은, 다른 사람들을 잘못된 길로 이끄는 많은 사람이 세상에 나왔기 때문입니다. 그들은 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 참사람으로 오셨다는 것을 분명히 말하려고 하지 않습니다. 그런 사람이 바로 미혹하는 자이며 적그리스도, 곧 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 원수입니다.

vi.L: Vì có nhiều kẻ lừa dối đã đi vào thế gian, là những kẻ không xưng nhận Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} đến trong xác thịt. Kẻ ấy là kẻ lừa dối và là kẻ chống Đấng Christ.
vi.B: Vì có nhiều kẻ lừa dối đã đi vào thế gian, là những người không xưng nhận Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} là Đấng đã đến trong xác thịt. Người như vậy là kẻ lừa dối và là kẻ chống Đấng Christ.
vi.R: Điều này rất quan trọng, vì có nhiều kẻ dẫn người khác đi lạc đã đi vào thế gian. Họ không chịu công khai nói rằng Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} đã đến như một con người thật. Người như vậy là kẻ lừa dối và là kẻ chống Đấng Christ, kẻ thù của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.

pt.L: Porque muitos enganadores saíram para o mundo, os que não confessam Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} vindo em carne. Este é o enganador e o anticristo.
pt.B: Pois muitos enganadores saíram pelo mundo, pessoas que não confessam Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} como aquele que veio em carne. Uma pessoa assim é o enganador e o anticristo.
pt.R: Isso é importante, porque muitas pessoas que desviam os outros do caminho certo saíram pelo mundo. Elas não querem dizer abertamente que Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} veio como um ser humano de verdade. Uma pessoa assim é o enganador e o anticristo, o inimigo {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}}.

am.L: ብዙ አሳቾች ወደ ዓለም ወጥተዋልና፤ እነርሱም በሥጋ የሚመጣውን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} በግልጥ የማይቀበሉ ናቸው። አሳቹና ፀረ ክርስቶሱ ይህ ነው።
am.B: ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በሥጋ እንደ መጣ በግልጥ የማይቀበሉ ብዙ አሳቾች ወደ ዓለም ወጥተዋልና። እንዲህ ያለው ሰው አሳቹና ፀረ ክርስቶሱ ነው።
am.R: ይህ አስፈላጊ ነው፤ ምክንያቱም ሰዎችን የሚያስቱ ብዙ ሰዎች ወደ ዓለም ወጥተዋል። ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} እውነተኛ ሰው ሆኖ እንደ መጣ በግልጥ አይናገሩም። እንዲህ ያለው ሰው አሳችና ፀረ ክርስቶስ፣ ማለትም {{christos:የክርስቶስ|የመሲሑ}} ጠላት ነው።

decisions.choice: for: the reason for holding to the command and the teaching
alternatives: "because" joined only to the last clause of verse 6
the start of a new thought, linked to the warning in verse 8
decisions.reason: ὅτι gives the reason behind verses 5-6: the readers must keep to what they heard from the beginning, because deceivers are abroad. The same reason leads into the warning of verse 8.

decisions.choice: deceivers: people who lead others astray
decisions.reason: πλάνος is one who causes others to wander from the truth. The verb from the same root is used of the false teachers in 1 John 2:26 and 3:7.

decisions.choice: have gone out into the world: they have left and are now at work
alternatives: have come into the world from outside
decisions.reason: The verb matches 1 John 4:1, where false prophets "have gone out into the world", and 1 John 2:19, where those who left "went out from us".

decisions.choice: do not confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh: the present participle names the incarnation as a lasting fact
alternatives: do not confess that Jesus Christ will come in the flesh (at his return)
the present tense as a timeless title, "the one who comes"
decisions.reason: 1 John 4:2 states the same confession with a perfect participle (ἔρχομαι in the form "having come"). Here the present participle ἐρχόμενον is best taken as naming the same fact without stressing time: Jesus Christ is the one who comes in the flesh, a real human being. A reference to his second coming in a body is possible but nothing in the letter points to it.

decisions.choice: the deceiver and the antichrist: each such person shows the character of the expected opponent of Christ
decisions.reason: οὗτός is singular but sums up the many just named, as in 1 John 2:22. The readers had been taught that the antichrist was coming; John says that the spirit of that opponent is already at work in those who deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh (1 John 2:18; 4:3).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "have gone out"
alternatives: "have entered" into the world (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a verb meaning "have entered"; the SBLGNT follows early manuscripts with "have gone out", the verb of 1 John 4:1. The sense is close. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: confess (L, B); openly say (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 4:2-3: to confess is to declare publicly what one holds true. Readable says plainly what it means.

decisions.choice: as one who has come in the flesh (B); came as a real human being (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the present participle (meaning decision m4) in the same words as 1 John 4:2. Literal keeps "coming" so that the reader can see the difference in form; the footnote explains it.

decisions.choice: antichrist, with no christos setting
decisions.reason: As in 1 John: "antichrist" is one established word. Readable explains it with "the enemy of Christ", where the setting does apply, as 1 John 2:18 does.

decisions.choice: This matters, because; people who lead others astray
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link with verses 5-6 a sentence of its own (meaning decision m1) and explains "deceivers" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: A person like that
decisions.reason: The singular sums up the many (meaning decision m5); "a person like that" says so, as 1 John 2:22 does at Readable.

decisions.choice: el anticristo, no christos span
decisions.reason: As in the English, "anticristo" is one word, the name of the expected opponent of Christ (m5), and the setting does not split it. Readable explains it as "el enemigo {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}", where the setting applies.

decisions.choice: trompeurs, le trompeur (L, B); des gens qui égarent les autres (R)
decisions.reason: The word is people who lead others astray (m2). "Séducteur" in modern French means a charmer in love; "trompeur" says deceit plainly.

decisions.choice: wapotoshaji, mpotoshaji
decisions.reason: The word is for people who lead others astray (m2). "Kupotosha" is to lead off the right way, while "kudanganya" is to tell lies, which is only part of it.

decisions.choice: mpinga-Kristo, no christos span
decisions.reason: As in the English, "mpinga-Kristo" is the name of the expected opponent of Christ (m5), and the setting does not split it. Readable explains it as "adui wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}", where the setting applies.

decisions.choice: "미혹하는 자"; "육신으로 오심" (L), "육신을 입고 오신" (B), "참사람으로 오셨다" (R); "적그리스도" with no christos span
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 4:2-3, with the same Korean for the same confession and the same antichrist. The meaning decision notes that the present participle names the incarnation as a lasting fact, and footnotes it; Korean "오심" (a noun) leaves the time open, as close as Korean can come.

decisions.choice: "kẻ chống Đấng Christ", with no christos span, as in 1 John 2:18
decisions.reason: The same fixed term as in 1 John for antichrist, which the English leaves without a setting; Readable explains it with the setting, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: vindo em carne (L); veio em carne (B); veio como um ser humano de verdade (R); o anticristo
decisions.reason: The same words as 1 John 4:2 in Portuguese, so the two confessions read alike; Literal keeps the present participle "vindo" so the difference in form (meaning decision m4) stays visible. "Anticristo" is lowercase with no title setting, as in 1 John 2:18, and Readable explains it under the setting.

decisions.choice: አሳቾች, አሳቹ (deceivers, the deceiver), from ማሳት (lead astray); ፀረ ክርስቶስ (antichrist) with no span, as in 1 John 2:18, explained at Readable
decisions.reason: A deceiver is one who leads others astray (meaning decision m2); "አሳች" is built on the verb of 1 John 2:26 and 3:7. "ፀረ ክርስቶስ" is the word settled in 1 John: a name made from the Greek, which keeps its form when the reader's setting changes "Christ" to "Messiah"; Readable explains it, and there the setting applies.

decisions.choice: በሥጋ የሚመጣውን (who comes in the flesh, L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present participle, which names the incarnation as a lasting fact (meaning decision m4); Balanced and Readable say "has come", as the English does and as 1 John 4:2 has it.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you" may lose what "we" worked for, and "you" receive the reward
alternatives: "we" may lose what "we" worked for and receive (many later manuscripts)
"you" may lose what "you" worked for (some early manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ over who is meant in the three verbs. Many later manuscripts have "we" throughout; some early manuscripts, including Codex Vaticanus as it is usually reported, have "you" throughout. The SBLGNT reads "you ... we ... you": the readers could lose what the elder and his fellow workers labored for among them. That mixed reading is the harder one, and copyists were more likely to make the persons match than to make them differ. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: we: the elder and those who brought the readers the truth
decisions.reason: The "we" who worked are set against "you" who could lose the result, so they are the witnesses and workers who first taught the readers (compare 1 John 1:1-4).

decisions.choice: a full reward: the whole of what God will give his faithful people, not a part of it
decisions.reason: μισθός is the wages or reward God gives (Matthew 5:12; 1 Corinthians 3:8, 14). The danger is losing part of it by being led astray; the verse does not say how much, and it does not make salvation a wage.

decisions.choice: watch yourselves: be on guard against being led astray
decisions.reason: βλέπετε with a reflexive pronoun means to look out for oneself (Mark 13:9). The plural speaks to every member.

decisions.choice: Look to yourselves
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek shape of verb and pronoun.

decisions.choice: what we have worked to bring about
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of work done and its result; Balanced names both.

decisions.choice: exclusive "chúng tôi" for "we worked"
decisions.reason: The "we" who worked are the elder and those who brought the readers the truth (m2), not the readers themselves, so Vietnamese uses the exclusive "chúng tôi".

decisions.choice: goes ahead: goes beyond the teaching, claiming to have moved past it
alternatives: leads others (as a leader goes in front)
decisions.reason: προάγω means to go before or go on ahead. Joined with "and does not remain", it describes someone who leaves the teaching behind, perhaps claiming a deeper knowledge. It may echo the false teachers' own claim to be advanced; the elder turns it into a charge.

decisions.choice: the teaching about Christ: what is taught about who he is
decisions.reason: The genitive can name Christ as the subject of the teaching or as its teacher. Verse 7 is about the confession of Jesus Christ, and verse 10 speaks of a visitor bringing "this teaching", which favors teaching about him. But John's Gospel speaks of Jesus' own teaching (John 7:16-17; 18:19), and the two are not far apart, since what Christ taught and what is taught about him agree.

decisions.choice: having God: knowing God and belonging to him; to have the Father one must have the Son
decisions.reason: The same language is in 1 John 2:23 and 5:12. Whoever lets go of the truth about the Son does not have God at all, whatever he claims.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "goes ahead", and "the teaching" without "of Christ" the second time
alternatives: "remains in the teaching of Christ" (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a verb meaning "transgresses" in place of "goes ahead", and add "of Christ" after the second "teaching". The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts with the shorter, harder reading. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: remain in the teaching: keep holding to it
decisions.reason: "Remain" is the word of 1 John 2:24-27: what the readers heard from the beginning must remain in them.

decisions.choice: goes too far (B); goes beyond (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what going ahead means here (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "goes ahead".

decisions.choice: the teaching about Christ
decisions.reason: Readable follows meaning decision m2. Literal and Balanced keep "of", which can carry either sense; the footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: is without God
decisions.reason: Natural English for "God he does not have", as 1 John 2:23 does at Balanced.

decisions.choice: enseñanza
decisions.reason: "Doctrina" suggests a fixed body of church teaching; the Greek word is the teaching that was given about Christ (m2), and "enseñanza" says that in everyday Spanish. "Permanecer" for remaining in it, as in John's Gospel and 1 John.

decisions.choice: anayetangulia mbele (L); anayevuka mipaka (B); anayepita zaidi ya (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is going ahead, claiming to have moved past the teaching (m1). Literal keeps "going ahead"; Balanced says "crossing the limits" and Readable "going beyond", as the English says "goes too far" and "goes beyond".

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 가르침" (L, B); "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에 관한 가르침" (R); "모시다" for having God, as in 1 John 2:23
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as the teaching about who Christ is, and footnotes the reading "Christ's own teaching". Literal and Balanced keep the open genitive; Readable follows the meaning decision, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "sự dạy dỗ của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" (L, B); "về" (R)
alternatives: "sự dạy dỗ về" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as the teaching about who Christ is (m2, uncertain). Literal and Balanced keep "của", which, like the Greek, can mean either the teaching Christ gave or the teaching about him; Readable says "về", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: permanece, at every level
decisions.reason: "Permanecer" as in 1 John 2:24-27 and John 15 in Portuguese (meaning decision m5), so the link with the first letter stays visible.

decisions.choice: ቀድሞ የሚሄድ (goes ahead, L), ከልክ አልፎ የሚሄድ (goes too far, B, R); {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሑ}} ትምህርት (in the teaching of Christ, L), {{christos:ስለ ክርስቶስ|ስለ መሲሑ}} የተሰጠው ትምህርት (the teaching about Christ, B, R)

The Greek genitive is read as teaching about who Christ is (m2), which Balanced and Readable say; the definite form "መሲሑ" follows the Greek article, and the whole word goes in each option.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone comes to you and this the teaching not brings, not receive him into house and to-rejoice to him not say;

en.L: If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive {{gender:them|him}} into [the] house, and do not say "Greetings" to {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: If anyone comes to you without bringing this teaching, do not receive {{gender:that person|him}} into your home, and do not give {{gender:them|him}} a greeting.
en.R: Someone may come to you who does not bring this teaching. If so, do not invite {{gender:that person|him}} into your home, and do not welcome {{gender:them|him}} with a greeting.

es.L: Si alguien llega a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y no trae esta enseñanza, no lo {{plural_you:acojan|acojáis}} en casa ni le {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: «Saludos».
es.B: Si alguien viene a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin traer esta enseñanza, no lo {{plural_you:reciban|recibáis}} en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} casa ni le {{plural_you:den|deis}} el saludo.
es.R: Puede ser que alguien venga a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin traer esta enseñanza. Si es así, no lo {{plural_you:inviten|invitéis}} a entrar en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} casa, ni le {{plural_you:den|deis}} la bienvenida con un saludo.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un vient à vous et n’apporte pas cet enseignement, ne le recevez pas dans la maison et ne lui dites pas : « Je te salue. »
fr.B: Si quelqu’un vient à vous sans apporter cet enseignement, ne le recevez pas chez vous et ne lui adressez pas de salutation.
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut venir vous voir sans apporter cet enseignement. Dans ce cas, ne l’invitez pas chez vous, et ne l’accueillez pas en le saluant.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote akija kwenu na haleti mafundisho haya, msimpokee nyumbani, wala msimwambie, "Salamu."
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akija kwenu bila kuleta mafundisho haya, msimpokee nyumbani mwenu, wala msimsalimu.
sw.R: Huenda mtu akaja kwenu ambaye haleti mafundisho haya. Ikiwa hivyo, msimkaribishe nyumbani mwenu, wala msimpokee kwa salamu.

ko.L: 누가 여러분에게 와서 이 가르침을 가져오지 않으면, 그를 집에 맞아들이지 말고, 그에게 인사도 하지 마십시오.

ko.R: 이 가르침을 가지고 오지 않는 사람이 여러분에게 찾아올 수도 있습니다. 그런 사람을 여러분의 집에 맞아들이지 말고, 반갑게 맞이하는 인사도 하지 마십시오.

vi.L: Nếu có ai đến với anh chị em mà không mang theo sự dạy dỗ này, thì đừng tiếp người ấy vào nhà, và đừng chào mừng người ấy;
vi.B: Nếu có ai đến với anh chị em mà không mang theo sự dạy dỗ này, thì đừng tiếp người ấy vào nhà mình, và đừng chào đón người ấy.

pt.L: Se alguém vem até vocês e não traz este ensino, não {{gender:recebam essa pessoa|o recebam}} em casa, e não lhe digam "Saudações".
pt.B: Se alguém vem até vocês sem trazer este ensino, não {{gender:recebam essa pessoa|o recebam}} em sua casa, nem lhe façam uma saudação.
pt.R: Pode ser que alguém venha até vocês sem trazer este ensino. Nesse caso, não convidem {{gender:essa pessoa|esse homem}} para entrar na casa de vocês, e não {{gender:a|o}} recebam com uma saudação.

am.L: ማንም ወደ እናንተ ቢመጣ ይህንም ትምህርት ባያመጣ፣ ወደ ቤት አትቀበሉት፤ «ሰላም» ደግሞ አትበሉት።
am.B: ማንም ይህን ትምህርት ሳያመጣ ወደ እናንተ ቢመጣ፣ ወደ ቤታችሁ አትቀበሉት፤ ሰላምታም አትስጡት።
am.R: ይህን ትምህርት ያላመጣ ሰው ወደ እናንተ ሊመጣ ይችላል። እንዲህ ከሆነ ወደ ቤታችሁ አትጋብዙት፤ ሰላምታ ሰጥታችሁም አትቀበሉት።

decisions.choice: a travelling teacher coming to the church, who was given lodging in a believer's house where the church met
alternatives: any visitor to a private home
decisions.reason: The churches met in homes (Romans 16:5; Colossians 4:15; Philemon 2), and travelling teachers and missionaries depended on believers for food, lodging and help on their way (3 John 5-8; Didache 11-12). "Comes to you" and "brings this teaching" describe such a visitor arriving to teach. To take him into the house was to give him a base and a hearing in the church.

decisions.choice: the greeting: the welcome that receives someone as a fellow believer and backs his mission
alternatives: any polite word to a person
decisions.reason: χαίρειν was the everyday greeting, "rejoice" or "greetings" (Acts 15:23; James 1:1). Spoken to a visiting teacher, it accepted him. Verse 11 gives the reason: such a welcome shares in his work.

decisions.choice: what the command does and does not forbid
alternatives: a command to refuse all contact or kindness to anyone in error
decisions.reason: The command is about a teacher who comes to spread a denial that Jesus Christ came in the flesh (verse 7). It forbids giving him the hospitality and welcome that would support his teaching. It does not speak of ordinary kindness to unbelievers, of neighbors or family who disagree, or of conversation that seeks to win someone back. The present imperatives make it a standing rule for the church.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the whole church
decisions.reason: The pronoun and both commands are plural (see verse 6).

decisions.choice: them/him through the gender setting
decisions.reason: The visitor is "anyone" (τις); the masculine pronoun is the Greek default for such a person. The setting gives the traditional form.

decisions.choice: your home
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article; English needs one. The home is the reader's own, where the church may meet (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: say "Greetings" (L); give a greeting (B); welcome with a greeting (R)
decisions.reason: The infinitive "to rejoice" was the standard greeting; "Greetings" is its English match. Readable adds "welcome" to show what the greeting meant (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: lo, le, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Lo" and "le" refer back to "alguien", which already covers men and women, and "le" does not change with gender, so Spanish needs no counterpart to the English spans "them|him" here or in verse 11.

decisions.choice: "quelqu’un … le, lui" with no gender span (verses 10-11)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:them|him}} for the pronoun; French "quelqu’un" already means anyone, and the "le" and "lui" that refer back to it are ordinary generic French, so no span is added (style guide §7).

decisions.choice: « Je te salue » (L); ne lui adressez pas de salutation (B); ne l’accueillez pas en le saluant (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek infinitive "rejoice" was the ordinary greeting; "Réjouis-toi" would be understood as an exhortation and "Salut" is too casual. "Je te salue" is the formal French greeting.

decisions.choice: mtu; -m- in the verb, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" means any person, and the object marker "-m-" ("msimpokee") does not mark gender, so Swahili has no counterpart to the English spans "them|him" here or in verse 11.

decisions.choice: "인사" (L); "환영 인사" (B); "반갑게 맞이하는 인사" (R), here and in verse 11
decisions.reason: The greeting is the welcome that receives someone as a fellow believer and backs his mission (meaning decision, with a footnote on what the command does and does not forbid). Balanced and Readable say it is a greeting of welcome, so the command is not read as forbidding ordinary courtesy.

decisions.choice: "chào mừng" (L), "chào đón" (B, R) for the greeting
decisions.reason: The greeting is the welcome that receives someone as a fellow believer and backs his mission (m2), not ordinary courtesy; "chào đón" says a welcome, where "chào hỏi" would be only saying hello.

decisions.choice: "Saudações"
decisions.reason: The Greek infinitive was the everyday greeting (meaning decision m2); "Saudações" is its Portuguese match, as the English Literal says "Greetings". "Alegra-te" copies the word but no one greets that way, and "Salve" sounds Latin or slangy. The pronoun "lhe" has no gender, so only the object of "receber" takes a span.

decisions.choice: «ሰላም» አትበሉት (do not say "Peace" to him, L); ሰላምታ አትስጡት (do not greet him, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek greeting word means "rejoice", the everyday hello; the Amharic everyday greeting is "ሰላም", so Literal quotes it, as the English Literal quotes "Greetings". The greeting is the welcome that receives someone as a fellow believer (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: አትቀበሉት, አትበሉት (him), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Amharic speaks of anyone in general with the ordinary singular (ማንም, ሰው, the verb and suffix of 'he'), heard as any person, man or woman, so there is no second wording for the setting to switch to; this holds for verse 11.

source.text: ὁ λέγων γὰρ αὐτῷ χαίρειν κοινωνεῖ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ τοῖς πονηροῖς.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] saying for to him to-rejoice shares in the works of him the evil.

en.L: For the one who says "Greetings" to {{gender:them|him}} shares in {{gender:their|his}} evil works.
en.B: For whoever gives {{gender:such a person|him}} a greeting becomes a partner in {{gender:their|his}} evil deeds.
en.R: Anyone who welcomes {{gender:such a person|him}} is taking part in the evil things {{gender:they do|he does}}.

es.L: Porque quien le dice «Saludos» tiene parte en sus obras malas.
es.B: Porque quien le da el saludo se hace cómplice de sus malas acciones.
es.R: Cualquiera que le da la bienvenida está tomando parte en el mal que esa persona hace.

fr.L: Car celui qui lui dit : « Je te salue » prend part à ses œuvres mauvaises.
fr.B: Car celui qui le salue se rend complice de ses mauvaises actions.
fr.R: Celui qui l’accueille prend part au mal qu’il fait.

sw.L: Kwa maana anayemwambia "Salamu" anashiriki katika matendo yake maovu.
sw.B: Kwa maana anayemsalimu mtu wa namna hiyo anakuwa mshirika katika matendo yake maovu.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote anayemkaribisha mtu wa namna hiyo anashiriki katika mambo maovu anayoyafanya.

ko.L: 그에게 인사하는 사람은 그의 악한 행위에 참여하는 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그런 사람에게 환영 인사를 하는 사람은 그의 악한 행위에 동참하는 것입니다.
ko.R: 그런 사람을 반갑게 맞이하는 사람은 그가 하는 악한 일에 함께하는 것입니다.

vi.L: vì ai chào mừng người ấy là dự phần vào những việc ác của người ấy.
vi.B: Vì ai chào đón người như thế là trở thành đồng phạm trong những việc ác của người ấy.
vi.R: Ai chào đón người như thế là đang góp phần vào những điều ác người ấy làm.

pt.L: Pois quem lhe diz "Saudações" participa das obras más {{gender:dessa pessoa|dele}}.
pt.B: Pois quem cumprimenta {{gender:uma pessoa assim|um homem assim}} se torna participante das más obras {{gender:dela|dele}}.
pt.R: Quem dá as boas-vindas a {{gender:uma pessoa assim|um homem assim}} está participando do mal que {{gender:ela faz|ele faz}}.

am.B: ለእንዲህ ያለው ሰው ሰላምታ የሚሰጥ በክፉ ሥራው ተባባሪ ይሆናልና።
am.R: እንዲህ ያለውን ሰው የሚቀበል ሁሉ እርሱ በሚሠራው ክፉ ነገር ተካፋይ ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: shares in: becomes a partner in
decisions.reason: κοινωνέω is the verb of fellowship (compare 1 John 1:3, 6-7). Welcoming the false teacher makes one a partner in spreading his teaching.

decisions.choice: his evil works: leading believers away from the truth about Christ
decisions.reason: In context the evil work is the deceiving of verse 7.

decisions.choice: welcomes
decisions.reason: Readable says what the greeting meant (verse 10, meaning decision m2) and leaves out "for", since the sentence plainly gives the reason.

source.text: Πολλὰ ἔχων ὑμῖν γράφειν οὐκ ἐβουλήθην διὰ χάρτου καὶ μέλανος, ἀλλὰ ἐλπίζω γενέσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ στόμα πρὸς στόμα λαλῆσαι, ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν πεπληρωμένη ᾖ.

records.literal_gloss: Many things having to you to write, not I wished through paper and ink, but I hope to come to you and mouth to mouth to speak, so that the joy of you having been made complete may be.

en.L: Having many things to write to you, I did not want [to do so] by means of paper and ink, but I hope to come to you and speak mouth to mouth, so that your joy may be made complete.
en.B: There is a great deal I could write to you, but I chose not to do it with paper and ink. I hope instead to come to you and speak with you face to face, so that your joy may be complete.
en.R: I have many more things to tell you, but I do not want to write them in a letter. I hope to visit you and talk with you in person. Then your joy will be full.

es.L: Teniendo muchas cosas que escribir{{plural_you:les|os}}, no quise [hacerlo] por medio de papel y tinta, sino que espero estar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y hablar de viva voz, para que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alegría quede completa.
es.B: Tengo mucho que podría escribir{{plural_you:les|os}}, pero preferí no hacerlo con papel y tinta. Espero, en cambio, ir a ver{{plural_you:los|os}} y hablar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en persona, para que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alegría sea completa.
es.R: Tengo muchas cosas más que contar{{plural_you:les|os}}, pero no quiero escribirlas en una carta. Espero visitar{{plural_you:los|os}} y hablar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en persona. Así {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alegría será plena.

fr.L: Ayant beaucoup de choses à vous écrire, je n’ai pas voulu [le faire] avec du papier et de l’encre, mais j’espère venir auprès de vous et parler de vive voix, afin que votre joie soit rendue complète.
fr.B: J’aurais beaucoup de choses à vous écrire, mais j’ai préféré ne pas le faire avec du papier et de l’encre. J’espère plutôt venir vous voir et vous parler face à face, pour que votre joie soit complète.
fr.R: J’ai encore beaucoup de choses à vous dire, mais je ne veux pas les écrire dans une lettre. J’espère venir vous voir et vous parler en personne. Alors votre joie sera entière.

sw.L: Nikiwa na mambo mengi ya kuwaandikia, sikutaka [kufanya hivyo] kwa karatasi na wino, bali natumaini kufika kwenu na kusema mdomo kwa mdomo, ili furaha yenu ikamilike.
sw.B: Kuna mambo mengi ambayo ningeweza kuwaandikia, lakini nimeamua kutoyaandika kwa karatasi na wino. Badala yake natumaini kuja kwenu na kuzungumza nanyi ana kwa ana, ili furaha yenu iwe kamili.
sw.R: Nina mambo mengi zaidi ya kuwaambia, lakini sitaki kuyaandika katika barua. Natumaini kuwatembelea na kuongea nanyi uso kwa uso. Hapo furaha yenu itakuwa tele.

ko.L: 내가 여러분에게 쓸 것이 많지만, 종이와 먹으로 쓰고 싶지 않았습니다. 오히려 여러분에게 가서 입과 입을 마주하고 말하기를 바랍니다. 그래서 여러분의 기쁨이 가득 차게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 여러분에게 쓸 것이 많지만, 종이와 먹으로 쓰지 않기로 했습니다. 그 대신 여러분에게 가서 얼굴을 마주하고 이야기하기를 바랍니다. 그러면 여러분의 기쁨이 가득 찰 것입니다.
ko.R: 여러분에게 할 말이 아직 많지만, 편지로 쓰고 싶지는 않습니다. 여러분을 찾아가서 직접 만나 이야기하기를 바랍니다. 그러면 여러분의 기쁨이 가득 찰 것입니다.

vi.L: Dù có nhiều điều để viết cho anh chị em, tôi không muốn [viết] bằng giấy và mực, nhưng tôi hy vọng đến với anh chị em và nói chuyện miệng đối miệng, để niềm vui của anh chị em được trọn vẹn.
vi.B: Tôi còn nhiều điều muốn viết cho anh chị em, nhưng tôi không muốn dùng giấy và mực. Thay vào đó, tôi hy vọng sẽ đến thăm anh chị em và trò chuyện trực tiếp, để niềm vui của anh chị em được trọn vẹn.
vi.R: Tôi còn nhiều điều muốn nói với anh chị em, nhưng tôi không muốn viết ra trong thư. Tôi hy vọng sẽ đến thăm và nói chuyện tận mặt với anh chị em. Khi đó niềm vui của anh chị em sẽ được tràn đầy.

pt.L: Tendo muitas coisas para escrever a vocês, não quis [fazê-lo] por meio de papel e tinta, mas espero ir até vocês e falar face a face, para que a alegria de vocês seja completada.
pt.B: Tenho muitas coisas que poderia escrever a vocês, mas preferi não fazer isso com papel e tinta. Em vez disso, espero visitá-los e falar com vocês face a face, para que a alegria de vocês seja completa.
pt.R: Tenho muitas outras coisas para contar a vocês, mas não quero escrevê-las numa carta. Espero visitar vocês e conversar pessoalmente com vocês. Então a alegria de vocês vai ficar completa.
